planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade; this seed strain was selected for cold tolerance well beyond typical Fatsia japonica.

directions: This is a 2025 Juniper Level Botanic Garden and Plant Delights seed-grown introduction raised from the famously cold-tolerant European clone 'Moseri', whose parent plant has shrugged off temperatures well below 0°F. It carries the same bold, deeply lobed, glossy dark-green hand-shaped leaves as typical Japanese aralia, forming a rounded mound that reached roughly 5 feet tall and 7 feet wide in twelve years on the original plant. Globe-like white flower clusters appear in October, followed by black fruit that lingers into winter. Grow it in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade, where it tolerates dry shade better than most broadleaf evergreens.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; this northern Honshu clone is markedly more cold-hardy than typical Aucuba japonica.

directions: Honshu was collected from a cold, high-snowfall region of Honshu, Japan, and introduced to the trade by Camellia Forest Nursery as a female clone of the northern botanical variety borealis, the most winter-hardy group within Aucuba japonica. It forms a compact clump clothed in glossy, serrated, evergreen leaves roughly 6 inches long, noticeably narrower than those of mainstream gold-dust type aucubas. Plant it with a male aucuba nearby to enjoy a crop of bright red berries through winter. Because it hails from a much snowier, colder part of Japan than the typical seed-grown species, it reliably survives in gardens well north of the usual aucuba range.

common_name: Male Man Aucuba (Cold-Hardy Pollinator Spotted Laurel)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; keep a specimen nearby to pollinate female aucubas for berry set.

directions: Male Man is a male-flowering clone of the cold-hardy northern Japanese botanical variety borealis, introduced by Juniper Level Botanic Garden as a compact, more weather-tough pollinator for female Aucuba selections. It flowers and sheds pollen each spring but never sets its own fruit, since only female plants bear the familiar red or yellow berries. At a mature height of only about 3 feet, it is notably smaller and tidier than most garden aucubas, with the same glossy, dark evergreen foliage and tolerance of deep, dry shade. Site it within range of female plants if berry production matters to your design.

common_name: Bored Female Aucuba (Cold-Hardy Black-Green Spotted Laurel)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; pair with a male aucuba nearby for a fruit set.

directions: Bored Female is another selection of the cold-hardy northern Japanese variety borealis from Juniper Level Botanic Garden, grown for its unusually shiny, nearly black-green evergreen foliage that reads darker than almost any other aucuba in cultivation. The clone was originally distributed under a male name but, once it flowered, proved to be female, earning its present name after the reclassification. It forms an elegant, dense mound to about 4 feet tall and wide, and will produce red berries where a male aucuba flowers nearby. Like other borealis selections, it tolerates far colder winters than the typical seed-grown Aucuba japonica sold in the trade.
